A1.justification: Both PDFs describe Heterogeneous Swarms and contain readable methods, equations, experiments, figures, tables, and appendices. Retained content can be matched despite substantial reformatting and renumbering.

before.justification: v1 reports original evaluations across 12 tasks, role/weight ablations, scaling and diversity experiments, and additional appendix results.

after.justification: v2 retains these empirical results and adds baseline evaluations, WikiDYK transfer results, and comparisons involving larger and mixed-size models.

M1.justification: The PSO updates, G-decode procedure, JFK-score, and alternating role/weight optimization remain unchanged. The new mixed-size experiment uses the role-only option already described in v1's Impact Statement; it does not introduce a new method component.

E1.justification: The original 12-task coverage remains. v2 adds WikiDYK as a held-out evaluation task after optimization on Knowledge Crosswords (Table 6), extending coverage within the existing encyclopedic-knowledge domain.

E2.justification: Table 1 adds evaluated AgentVerse and MACNet baselines. Appendix C additionally compares against single Gemma-2-27B and Gemma-3-27B models and chain-of-thought and graph-of-thought reasoning. Prediction ensemble and Uniform Soup also newly participate in the collaborative-gain comparison, although they already appeared in v1's main evaluation.

E3.justification: The retained experiments keep their splits, metrics, and search settings. New designs include optimizing on Knowledge Crosswords and testing on WikiDYK, comparing three Gemma-2-9B models or six Gemma-3-4B models against larger single models, and evaluating role-only collaboration with mixed 7B/2B models. These substantially expand the evaluation protocols.

E4.justification: Appendix C adds tests of transfer to an unseen task, mixed-size collaboration, comparisons at similar total parameter counts, enhanced single-model reasoning controls, and baseline collaborative gains (Tables 6–7 and Figures 10–12). The earlier ablations, sparsity, diversity, dropout, scaling, and qualitative analyses are retained.

E5.justification: Both versions report the same one-tailed z-test procedure and significance annotations in v1 Table 5 and v2 Table 8. The stated 50–200 hyperparameter-search trials are unchanged, and v2 adds no repeated-seed uncertainty estimates, confidence intervals, or error-bar reporting.

E6.justification: Every shared Table 1 result remains unchanged, but v2 adds AgentVerse and MACNet rows and substantial new results in Tables 6–7 and Figures 10–12. For example, the newly reported WikiDYK transfer score is 0.566 for Heterogeneous Swarms versus 0.527 for Model Swarms. These are additional comparisons and settings, not improvements over v1 under unchanged conditions.

T1.justification: v2 Table 4 extends the analytical cost discussion to baseline families, including nN optimization calls for dynamic-role approaches versus n(N+M) for Heterogeneous Swarms. The existing mathematical definitions, optimization equations, DAG reasoning, and complexity analysis of the proposed method remain unchanged; no new proofs are added.

C1.justification: The abstract and conclusion broaden the comparative claim from outperforming 15 baselines to 17, although the introduction still says 15. The central contribution of joint role/weight optimization and the headline 18.5% improvement across 12 tasks remain unchanged.

C2.justification: v2 adds interpretations concerning transfer, smaller-model teams, mixed-size collaboration, and why additional optimization cost is justified. Some conclusions are overbroad: Table 7's mixed-size team trails the single 7B model on Knowledge Crosswords and NLGraph despite the accompanying superiority statement. Most limitations are retained from v1 and merely relocated.

D1.justification: v2 adds a repository resource pointer and discloses a cluster of 16 A100 GPUs with 40 GB each. Existing prompts, preprocessing, hyperparameter ranges, and baseline implementation descriptions are retained. Detailed implementation information for the newly added baselines and appendix experiments remains limited.

R1.justification: v2 substantially expands the cited multi-agent and agentic-systems literature in Section 7 and Appendices A–B, including AgentVerse, MACNet, AFlow, AgentDojo, and AgentHarm, and adds chain-of-thought and graph-of-thought references. The underlying positioning around role-based versus weight-based collaboration remains stable.

P1.justification: Most prose and the main Sections 1–8 retain their organization. Changes include local wording and explanatory additions, splitting the Impact Statement into appendix Limitations and Ethics sections, moving G-decode pseudocode to the appendix, and adding acknowledgements and the NeurIPS checklist.

P2.justification: The document changes from a two-column format to a predominantly single-column NeurIPS layout, with extensive resizing and relocation of figures, tables, and algorithms. v2 adds Figures 10–12 and Tables 4, 6, and 7, expands Table 1, and renumbers the retained appendix displays.

improvement.justification: The added reasoning and model-size controls, baseline collaborative-gain comparisons, and WikiDYK transfer experiment strengthen evidence beyond v1's task-specific evaluation. Hardware disclosure also improves documentation. The gains are limited by sparse details for new experiments and overbroad interpretations, particularly the mixed-size superiority statement contradicted on two tasks by Table 7. The core method and main results remain stable.
